planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; 'Arnold Promise' blooms in late winter while dormant, so plant it where its bare, flower-studded branches can be seen from the house on gray winter days.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; 'Arnold Promise' blooms in late winter while dormant, so plant it where its bare, flower-studded branches can be seen from the house on gray winter days. Hamamelis x intermedia 'Arnold Promise' is one of the most celebrated winter-blooming shrubs, a cross between Chinese and Japanese witch hazel selected at the Arnold Arboretum for its abundant clusters of spidery, ribbon-petaled, bright yellow flowers that open in late winter, often while snow is still on the ground, followed by good yellow-orange fall foliage color. It is among the latest-blooming and most floriferous witch hazel cultivars, providing months of anticipation-breaking color in a shaded winter border when almost nothing else is in flower. Prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, and give it consistently moist, well-drained soil, since witch hazel resents both drought and waterlogging.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; paperbush sets its silvery, silky flower buds in fall and holds them ornamentally through winter before opening in late winter, so avoid pruning after midsummer or next year's display will be lost.

directions: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; paperbush sets its silvery, silky flower buds in fall and holds them ornamentally through winter before opening in late winter, so avoid pruning after midsummer or next year's display will be lost. Edgeworthia chrysantha is a striking Asian shrub with a distinctive tiered, architectural branching structure and large, soft, blue-green leaves, producing rounded clusters of intensely fragrant, tubular, golden-yellow flowers that open from silvery, fur-covered buds in late winter to earliest spring before the leaves emerge. Its combination of bold winter structure, ornamental buds held through the cold months, and richly fragrant late-winter bloom makes it a premier specimen shrub for a shaded winter garden, best sited near a path or entrance where its fragrance can be appreciated. The bark has traditionally been used to make high-quality paper in Japan and China, giving the plant its common name, and it prefers a sheltered site out of harsh winter wind at the colder edge of its hardiness range.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; early stachyurus sets its dangling flower chains in fall and displays them through winter before opening, so prune only right after flowering to avoid removing next year's buds.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade; early stachyurus sets its dangling flower chains in fall and displays them through winter before opening, so prune only right after flowering to avoid removing next year's buds. Stachyurus praecox is a graceful Japanese shrub with arching, reddish-brown branches that hang with drooping chains of small, pale yellow, bell-shaped flowers in late winter to early spring, opening from buds that form the previous fall and remain an ornamental feature through the cold months. Its arching form and cascading winter flower chains make it a distinctive specimen for a shaded border, adding a different texture and bloom form than the more upright witch hazel or paperbush that flower at the same season. It appreciates the same acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist soil favored by camellia and rhododendron, and benefits from a sheltered site out of harsh winter wind.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade; fragrant winterhazel blooms before its leaves emerge in early spring, so site it where the drooping, fragrant flower chains can be seen against a dark evergreen backdrop.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade; fragrant winterhazel blooms before its leaves emerge in early spring, so site it where the drooping, fragrant flower chains can be seen against a dark evergreen backdrop. Corylopsis glabrescens is a large, rounded Japanese shrub producing drooping chains of small, soft yellow, sweetly fragrant, bell-shaped flowers in early spring before the rounded, blue-green leaves unfurl, followed by attractive yellow fall color. It is among the most cold-hardy and heat-tolerant of the winterhazels, making it a dependable large specimen or informal hedge for a shaded border where its fragrant early bloom announces the start of spring. Give it the same acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist soil favored by azalea and rhododendron, and prune only right after flowering, since it blooms on the previous year's wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; white enkianthus stays more compact than redvein enkianthus and works well as a foundation shrub or low hedge in an acidic-soil shade garden.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; white enkianthus stays more compact than redvein enkianthus and works well as a foundation shrub or low hedge in an acidic-soil shade garden. Enkianthus perulatus is a compact Japanese shrub with fine-textured foliage and clusters of small, pure white, urn-shaped flowers dangling beneath the branches in mid-spring, followed by outstanding fall color that ranges from bright red to orange-scarlet, among the most reliable fall foliage displays of any acidic-soil shrub. Its smaller size compared with redvein enkianthus makes it a good fit for foundation plantings, low hedges, or the middle layer of an azalea and rhododendron border in partial shade. It needs the same acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist soil as its relatives and requires little pruning beyond removing any dead or crossing branches.
